* Coordinate trademark registration, renewals and brand protection activities.
* Review agreements relating to trademarks, product formulations, packaging, designs, marketing materials and other intellectual property.

* Ability to work independently and provide practical, business-oriented advice.

title: Specialist - Commercial Standards Claims & Contract
description:
**Job Description**
**Specialist — Commercial Standards, Claims & Contracts is a Business Analyst and SME on the Customer Operations Transformation programme.**
The outcome is a clear, governed set of commercial policies — credit, claims, pricing and trade terms — and customer agreements that are standard, compliant and correctly executed in the systems; fewer and cleaner customer claims; lower invalid deductions and trade-spend leakage; and <1 Day Resolution wherever the process allows: fewer claims arising in the first place, and faster, controlled settlement for those that remain. Everything this role does serves that outcome.
  
  
The scope spans Commercial Standards, Claims and Contracts end to end — formulation and governance of credit, claims, pricing and trade-terms policies, policy exceptions and delegation of authority, the customer agreement and contract lifecycle (drafting, approval, activation, amendment and renewal), pricing, rebate, discount and promotion setup, accruals, claims intake, validation and settlement, proof of performance, and the controls that link agreed terms to what is invoiced and paid. The role designs across this scope as one process rather than as separate contract, promotion and claims solutions. It works with market Commercial, Revenue Growth Management, Sales Finance, Credit, Legal, Internal Control, Customer Service and Collections teams, GBO, D&T, the SAP and Control Tower (Claims and Deduction platform) teams and third-party vendors.
  
  
The role combines 5 capabilities in one person. As an SME, they formulate, document the global commercial policies — credit policy (credit limits, payment terms, risk categories, blocks and releases), claims policy (eligibility, evidence, time limits, approval and write-off thresholds), and pricing governance (price-setting and approval, discount and rebate guardrails, price-change control) — and the standards and controls that make them work in practice. As a business analyst, they interrogate contract, trade-terms, accrual, claims and deduction data, document current and target process, and write requirements to standard. As a subject matter expert, they bring the functional depth to act as design authority for the fragment and to challenge solutions that would not work in the markets. As a sprint or project owner, they take a scope fragment through design, test and deployment on a two to four week value drop cadence. As a process and technology expert, they translate commercial policy, contract terms and controls into working design on SAP pricing, condition contracts and settlement management, Control Tower claims and deduction capability, and the contract and trade promotion management toolset.
  
  
**The defining discipline of this role is designing claims out at source, not processing them faster.**
A quicker claim approval is a smaller prize than a contract term clear enough never to be disputed; a faster settlement is a smaller prize than a promotion set up correctly in the system so the customer never needs to claim. The postholder is expected to use the data to find where in the commercial process claims are created — an ambiguous contract clause, a non-standard trade term, a late or incorrect pricing or promotion setup, an accrual gap, a weak approval control — and design the fix upstream into commercial policy, standards, contract templates, deal approval and master data, as well as into the claims and settlement design.
  
  
**Understanding of markets and of upstream and downstream impact is central to the role.**
A claim usually starts life as a commercial negotiation; a contract term becomes a pricing condition, an accrual, an invoice and, if anything is misaligned, a deduction in Collections. The postholder is expected to know what happens on either side of their own process — from deal negotiation through to cash and the P&L — and to design accordingly.
  
  
**This is a transformation design and delivery role, not an operational one.**
The postholder does not negotiate customer deals, draft or approve individual contracts, validate or settle individual claims, or manage customer relationships; that stays with market Commercial, Legal, GBO and BPO run teams. The role changes how that work is done — including the commercial policies, standards, contract templates, reason codes, analytics and controls that let run teams find and remove causes in BAU. The role formulates and recommends policy; final approval sits with the relevant policy owners and governance forums.
  
  
The role works independently within an agreed frame set by the workstream lead, gathers its own data, forms its own view and brings recommendations rather than questions. Where a Senior Specialist is assigned on the same fragment, it works under their design direction. Decisions are expected to be based on evidence rather than opinion, and every artefact is expected to meet the programme documentation, taxonomy and quality standards, including BPQMS.
  
  
**Analyse commercial terms, contracts and claims performance and baseline the problem — 25%.**
Document current-state credit, claims and pricing policies, commercial standards, contract lifecycle and claims processes across markets and identify variation from the global standard. Build the process, trade-terms and claim-type taxonomy and interrogate the data directly at portfolio level — customer agreements and terms, pricing and promotion conditions, accruals versus actuals, claims volume, value, ageing and rejection rates, invalid deductions, write-offs and trade-spend leakage — to baseline the problem per market and size the opportunity. Perform gap analysis between current process, commercial policy, contract terms, platform capability, controls and the target operating model, separating structural design issues from operational backlog. Support business-rule validation, master-data requirements and policy analysis. Aim for validated current-state documentation and a defensible baseline that will stand up to audit.
  
  
**Formulate commercial policies and standards, and design claims out at source — 25%.**
Support future-state design aligned to the global standard, always designing for the cause rather than the symptom. Formulate, document and maintain the global commercial policies the design depends on — credit policy (credit limits and risk categorisation, payment terms, credit blocks and release authority), claims policy (claim eligibility, evidence and proof-of-performance requirements, submission time limits, validation, approval and write-off thresholds) and pricing governance (price-setting and approval, discount, rebate and promotion guardrails, price-change control and margin protection) — with a clear policy-exception and delegation-of-authority framework, and take them through the governance forums for approval. Translate policy into the standards that operationalise it: standard trade-terms structures, contract and agreement templates, clause libraries, deal approval and delegation-of-authority rules, and the minimum data a contract must carry to be executed correctly in the systems. Use the baseline to show where claims are created — contract ambiguity, non-standard terms, pricing and promotion setup, accruals, proof of performance, master data — and design the fix upstream. Design the interventions: standard contract-to-condition setup, automated accruals and settlement, validated claim intake, reason-code frameworks and claims workflow. Prepare business requirements, functional specifications, process flows, business rules and user stories. Facilitate design workshops and document outcomes and decisions. Assess process, policy, financial and control impacts, and define how policy compliance will be monitored.
  
  
Deliver the outcome: standard contracts, fewer claims and <1 Day Resolution — 20%. Design for, and evidence, policy adoption and compliance across markets, an increase in contracts on standard terms and templates, fewer policy exceptions, a reduction in claims volume, aged claims, invalid deductions and trade-spend leakage, and movement toward <1 Day Resolution for appropriate claims and queries. Shape the build-out of SAP pricing, condition contracts and settlement management, Control Tower claims and deduction functionality, and contract and trade promotion management tooling as the primary levers on the outcome. Define the measures with the business owner, monitor post-go-live performance against the baseline, and recommend and, where owned, implement continuous improvements to the design. This is the accountability every other accountability serves.
  
  
**Own testing, deployment and adoption through the value drops — 20%.**
Translate requirements into working design on SAP, Control Tower and the contract and trade promotion management toolset with D&T, system integrators and vendors. Define and review test scenarios, support SIT and UAT, and manage defect resolution with business users. Break the work into fragments that can be delivered on the value drop cadence, and own the backlog, dependencies and risks for the fragment. Aim for SIT and UAT completed with minimal post-go-live defects and a clean handover into run.
  
  
**Manage delivery discipline and enable across the programme — 10%.**
Track requirements, risks, assumptions, dependencies and decisions throughout the lifecycle, and escalate early and precisely when the frame is wrong. Act as a trusted partner to market Commercial, Revenue Growth Management, Sales Finance, Credit, Legal, Internal Control, Customer Service, GBO, D&T and vendors, and coach business users through testing, deployment and adoption. Enable the adjacent workstreams — Order-to-Invoice, Collections, Claims & Receivables, Customer Service and Supply — by surfacing cross-boundary impact before it becomes a deployment defect, and by handing design-level root causes to the workstream that owns them.
  
  

* Commercial Standards, Claims & Contracts domain depth and business analysis, on a broad Customer Operations base. Real SME depth in commercial policy and customer contracts — credit policy and credit risk, claims policy, pricing governance, trade-terms structures, rebates, discounts and promotions, contract lifecycle management, accruals, and claims validation and settlement — sufficient to act as design authority and to write policy that is clear, enforceable and auditable, combined with strong business-analysis craft: process mapping, requirements gathering, gap analysis, functional-specification writing, user stories and workshop facilitation. Understands how claims and deductions are created across the commercial and Order to Cash process, and how contract wording, deal approval, pricing and promotion setup, master data and accruals drive them. Built on a general understanding of Customer Operations end-to-end (Order to Cash, Commercial and Supply) and of how markets actually work, including upstream and downstream impact. Knows Consumer Products industry standards and the realities of Beer, Wine & Spirits — distributor and wholesaler concentration, complex customer agreements, promotional and trade-spend claims, and route-to-market and regulatory constraints on trade terms. Working knowledge of Diageo BPQMS standards.
* Data, technology and delivery discipline. Comfortable interrogating contract, trade-terms, accrual, claims and deduction data directly, and translating requirements into working design on SAP pricing, condition contracts and settlement management, the Control Tower claims and deduction platform, and the supporting contract and trade promotion management toolset. Understands the platform, the data model, the business rules, workflow and approval logic, and the operating model — retained, GBO and BPO — beneath the process. Strong on test planning and defect management (SIT / UAT), business readiness and hypercare, and on risk, issue and dependency management. Data-driven by instinct — baselines the problem, quantifies the opportunity and lets the evidence settle the argument. Able to prioritise across concurrent workstreams and deadlines.
* Design-for-prevention rigour, stakeholder influence and adaptability. Relentless about cause over symptom in design — not satisfied with automating a workaround when the claim could be designed out through a clearer standard, contract or setup. Strong stakeholder management and influencing across a global and local matrix, including senior Commercial, Finance and Legal stakeholders and policy governance forums, and consultative by default: frames the problem before prescribing and drives stakeholders toward aligned design decisions. Clear communicator, and able to manage conflict to a resolution rather than let it stall a decision. Further your career at Ball, a world leader in manufacturing sustainable aluminium packaging. Achieve extraordinary things when you join our team, and make a difference in your professional development, the community, and around the globe!
  
  
Create a new future. Apply Today.
  
  
**Position Overview**
The Company Secretary (CS) is responsible for ensuring full compliance with statutory, legal, and regulatory requirements applicable to the organization. The role ensures effective corporate governance, supports the Board of Directors, manages secretarial records, ensures timely filings under the Companies Act, 2013 and related laws, and support corporate decision making.
  
  
The Company Secretary acts as a key link between the Board, senior management, regulators, auditors, and stakeholders. The role also oversees legal compliance, contract management, risk mitigation, and supports corporate initiatives such as mergers, expansions, and statutory audits.
  
  
Ensures that the company operates with the highest standards of governance, transparency, and ethical practices.
  
  
**Your Key Responsibilities Include**
**Corporate Governance & Board Management**

* Organize and document Board, Committee, and General Meetings as per Companies Act, 2013.
* Prepare agendas, notices, resolutions, and supporting papers.
* Maintain statutory registers and minutes (physical/electronic).
* Advise Board on governance, compliance, corporate responsibilities & secretarial practices.
* File statutory returns (AOC‑4, MGT‑7, DIR‑3 KYC, MSME, etc.) on time.

**Statutory & Regulatory Compliance**

* Ensure compliance with Companies Act, FEMA regulations, SEBI regulations (if applicable) etc
* Liaise with ROC, MCA, RBI, SEBI, and other regulators.
* Track legal changes and guide management on required actions.
* Manage CSR compliance, documentation, and committee support.

**Legal & Contract Management ( If Required )**

* Draft, review, and vet contracts, vendor agreements, NDAs, and service/purchase agreements.
* Maintain contract repository and manage renewals.
* Support legal matters, disputes, arbitration, in consultation with the Legal team.

**Secretarial & Documentation Control**

* Maintain statutory registers (Members, Directors, Charges, Contracts, etc.).
* Manage share certificates, transfers, and related records.
* Handle loan/charge documentation and coordinate with banks.

**Risk Management & Internal Controls**

* Identify compliance risks and implement mitigation measures.
* Support internal, statutory, and secretarial audits.
* Develop compliance checklists, SOPs, and internal control systems.
* Based on the company’s framework of Compliance Calendar - follow-up with respective teams for the confirmation of compliance of the Applicable Laws.
* Managing the Internal Compliance tool of the Company & preparing the monthly compliance chart.
* Providing the Financial Impact assessment of Non-Compliance of other corporate Laws to the Board.
* Review of Organization Approval Matrix and assessing the implementation of the Matrix and its functionality.

**Stakeholder Management**

* Act as primary contact for shareholders, regulators, auditors, and authorities.
* Support investor relations (if applicable).
* Coordinate with Finance, HR, Operations, EHS, and Procurement Teams for organization-wide compliance.

* Support M&A, JV, restructuring, and strategic initiatives.
* Draft policies, charters, and governance frameworks, in co-ordination with the Legal Team.

* Support insurance renewals and claims.
* Maintain confidentiality and be available during audits, inspections, and urgent compliance matters.

* Experience in handling Board meetings, statutory filings, and corporate governance.
* Exposure to contract management, legal documentation, and regulatory interactions.
* Experience in managing compliance for multi‑plant operations preferred.
* Strong knowledge of Companies Act, 2013, FEMA regulations, Labour Laws, and industrial regulations, and all applicable Corporate Laws.

* Excellent drafting, documentation, and communication skills.
* High integrity, confidentiality, and ethical judgment.
* Ability to manage multiple stakeholders and deadlines, and advice on corporate restructuring & governance.
* Proficiency in MCA portal, e‑filings, and MS Office.
* Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills.
* English (Proficient).
* Local language (preferred).

title: Operational Risk, Senior Associate
description:
Role Summary
  
  
State Street uses third parties to support internal processes and the delivery of products and services to clients. These relationships are evaluated and risk-assessed through the Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) Program.
  
  
The Third-Party Risk Management Associate will support the effective execution of activities across one or more TPRM lifecycle pillars. Depending on business requirements, the role may include reviewing TPRM cases and engagement records, reviewing and challenging inherent risk assessments, coordinating supplier due diligence outreach, monitoring and reviewing due diligence submissions, preparing executive summaries, and managing relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  
  
The successful candidate will apply sound risk judgement, identify and resolve data or process inconsistencies, maintain complete and accurate records, and communicate TPRM requirements and assessment outcomes clearly. The role requires close collaboration with Engagement Managers, third-party suppliers, risk-domain subject matter experts, Business Advisors, Procurement, Legal, and TPRM teams to support timely, consistent, policy-aligned, and audit-ready outcomes.
  
  
**Job Duties And Responsibilities**

* Develop and maintain a strong understanding of State Street’s business lines, products and services, third-party operating model, and TPRM lifecycle requirements.
* Review and evaluate TPRM SNOW cases, Archer engagement records, assessment records, and supporting documentation for completeness, accuracy, consistency, and compliance with applicable policies, standards and procedures
* Manage assigned case queues, review and effectively challenge TPRM cases and support business lines in faster onboarding of third-party suppliers.
* Identify inconsistencies or gaps in inherent risk questionnaire responses and work with Engagement Managers and relevant stakeholders to resolve issues before approval.
* Apply knowledge of inherent risk questionnaire logic, scoring, question interdependencies, and due diligence triggers to confirm that the resulting inherent risk rating and due diligence requirements are appropriate.
* Prepare and distribute due diligence questionnaires and supporting requirements to third-party suppliers or internal service providers within established timelines.
* Monitor due diligence progress, perform follow-ups and escalations, and maintain clear records of outreach, responses, decisions, and outstanding actions.
* Perform completeness and quality reviews of returned due diligence questionnaires and supporting artifacts before routing the assessment to the appropriate risk-domain subject matter experts.
* Coordinate follow-up questions, clarification discussions, and supplier meetings; track responses and facilitate resolution of outstanding items.
* Review and analyse due diligence results, assessment conclusions, control-effectiveness ratings, and identified findings to confirm that outcomes are sufficiently supported and accurately documented.
* Prepare clear, concise, and audit-ready executive summaries that communicate the engagement scope, inherent risk profile, due diligence results, control effectiveness, findings, residual concerns, and required acknowledgement or next steps.
* Coordinate executive-summary review and issuance with Engagement Managers, Executive Sponsors, Business Advisors, risk-domain subject matter experts, and other relevant stakeholders.
* Build and maintain effective working relationships with third-party suppliers, Engagement Managers, business stakeholders, Procurement, Legal, risk-domain subject matter experts, and TPRM partner teams.
* Explain TPRM requirements, risk-analysis conclusions, findings, and remediation expectations clearly and professionally, and guide stakeholders toward timely resolution.
* Ensure that TPRM decisions, approvals, exceptions, and supporting evidence are accurately captured in Archer and relevant repositories to support governance, audit, and regulatory review.
* Support the preparation of management information, metrics, trend analysis, and status reporting for TPRM leadership and governance forums.
* Maintain and enhance procedures, checklists, templates, job aids, frequently asked questions, and other process documentation.
* Identify opportunities to improve process efficiency, data quality, control effectiveness, stakeholder experience, and consistency of TPRM outcomes.
* Participate in system testing, process-change initiatives, remediation programmes, quality-assurance reviews, audits, and regulatory inspections.
* Maintain flexibility to work across TPRM pillars and support emerging programme priorities arising from business, regulatory, policy, technology, or operating-model changes.
* Perform all responsibilities in accordance with State Street’s risk appetite, policies, standards, ethical requirements, and control expectations.

**Skills**

* Strong knowledge of third-party risk management principles, lifecycle activities, and governance requirements within a regulated financial-services environment.
* Sound risk judgement and the ability to assess the reasonableness, completeness, and consistency of information and supporting evidence.
* Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to identify gaps, challenge assumptions, and develop practical resolution paths.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills
* Strong stakeholder and relationship-management skills, with the ability to influence outcomes while maintaining professional and constructive working relationships.
* Ability to manage multiple cases, competing priorities, and tight deadlines in a high-volume, control-focused environment.
* Strong organisational, documentation, and time-management skills, with close attention to detail.
* Strong customer-centric mindset and commitment to providing clear guidance and responsive support to business and supplier stakeholders.
* Strong proficiency in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and related reporting tools.
* Working knowledge of Archer or a comparable governance, risk, and compliance platform is preferred.
* High ethical standards, professional integrity, and commitment to maintaining appropriate confidentiality.

**Qualifications**

* Overall professional experience of 2 or more years, preferably within banking, financial services, risk management, compliance, procurement, audit, controls, or a related field.
* Relevant experience in Third-Party Risk Management, operational risk, supplier risk, vendor management, due diligence, or another risk-and-control function.
* Practical experience in one or more of the following areas is preferred: TPRM case review, inherent risk assessment, due diligence outreach and completeness review, risk assessment coordination, findings management, executive-summary preparation, or stakeholder relationship management.
* General knowledge of third-party risk domains, including Operational Resiliency, Operational Risk, Cybersecurity, Information Sensitivity and Access, Privacy, Physical Security, Reputational Risk, Compliance, Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Bribery and Corruption, Financial Viability, and Tax Evasion.
* Experience working with internal stakeholders, third-party suppliers, and subject matter experts in a matrixed and globally distributed organization.
* Experience preparing management reporting, governance materials, executive communications, audit evidence, or regulatory-response documentation is preferred.
* Bachelor’s degree in business or a postgraduate management qualification is preferred.
* Relevant professional certification such as CRVPM, CRISC, CISM, CISA, CBCI, or an equivalent risk-management qualification is advantageous.
* Prior experience with Archer or a comparable governance, risk, and compliance platform is preferred.
* Please note: The role is required to support internal clients during the first half of US working hours.

Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.
  
  
We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.
